subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Mercedes-Benz engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the OM642 across all six model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The OM642 is one of the broadest-application engines we work on - the same base V6 diesel across nine model lines, including high-mileage Sprinter vans and luxury passenger cars.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, oil cooler seals, and swirl flap linkage as standard on every rebuild - we treat these as known wear items rather than wait for failure. BlueTEC applications additionally account for the AdBlue system components.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: Confirmed issues include oil cooler seal failure (oil and coolant loss in the V of the engine), swirl flap linkage breakage (leading to limp mode), and VGT actuator linkage jamming. These are well-documented patterns, and we inspect and replace the relevant components as standard during a rebuild.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page - they'll be added once a documented set of completed OM642 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.
